transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (SummitBridge Channel Director), Ethan Brooks (SummitBridge Head of Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (SummitBridge Sales Director)

Summary (auto): Joint pipeline review and co-sell strategy. Align on top joint accounts, pilot approach (hosted vs dedicated), pricing guidance, legal/contract touchpoints, and next steps for exec intro and benchmarks.

Topics: pipeline motion, joint account mapping, compensation model, technical pilot scope, security/compliance gating (SOC2/KMS/SSO), competitive positioning

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time the week before xmas, um we'll try to keep this tight. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. Maya, Ethan, Liam, thanks for being here.
[00:12] Maya: Thanks Alex, yeah appreciate it. Quick heads up, call's on my side too — we're trying to move fast here.
[00:18] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. We'll go through the co-sell list, a couple of asks on pilots, and then talk comp/commissions.
[00:25] Ethan: Sounds good. The partnership team is mostly focused on how we hand off opportunities to field and how the comp looks.
[00:31] Liam: From Sales perspective, priority is which accounts are ready for joint outreach and what materials we get to take to meetings.
[00:37] Alex: Perfect. Starting with pipeline — Maya, can you run us through the top joint accounts you had in mind?
[00:45] Maya: Yeah — we've got about 12 accounts we think are co-sell-ready. Top three are NorthStar Health, Meridian Logistics, and AltaRetail. NorthStar is a big priority; they've got an internal A.I. initiative and they've asked about VPC/on-prem options.
[01:00] Priya: When you say VPC, do you mean Private deployment or just private networking to the hosted API?
[01:07] Maya: They want full VPC peering or an on-prem option if we can satisfy security — something like Redwood Private or an air-gapped setup.
[01:15] Alex: Got it. We support Private deployments and on-prem via the Private offering; there's some lead time but it's doable. We'll flag that as a technical gating item.
[01:23] Ethan: Any quick thoughts on competitive risk? NorthStar has also talked to Anthropic and a couple of hyperscalers.
[01:30] Priya: Competitively — Anthropic is often positioned on safety, and Vertex AI gets used because it's in their Google stack. We should emphasize Redwood's production-grade latency and cost controls — that resonates with procurement.
[01:40] Liam: We need a one-pager that compares Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private — with numbers on latency and typical unit cost. That's what gets the buyer's attention.
[01:49] Alex: We'll share an updated co-sell deck with a comparison table. Priya, can you include the perf matrix with sample latencies across sequence lengths?
[01:56] Priya: Yep, I'll include hosted and dedicated numbers, and call out KV cache and batching benefits; note — our internal tests show dedicated reduces p95 by about 30% for typical chat loads.
[02:08] Maya: Awesome. For pricing, our field wants commission ranges and also whether Redwood offers any partner acceleration credits for pilots.
[02:16] Alex: We can propose a pilot credit structure. I'll include a partner commission matrix in the deck.
[02:21] Ethan: On the legal side — what's the usual process for adding a partner addendum to the MSA? We want to know timeline.
[02:29] Alex: Typically we exchange partner contract contact, Redwood legal can draft an addendum. That usually takes 2–3 weeks depending on counterparty redlines. We'll share contacts.
[02:36] Liam: Good. Next — pilot scope. We recommended running pilots on 3 accounts: one is purely hosted API, one dedicated pool, and one private/VPC test for NorthStar. Priya, can you own the pilot plan?
[02:48] Priya: Yes — I'll draft a pilot plan specifying success metrics (latency p95 < 300ms for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens target, and qualitative evals). Also include fallback model variants and rollout criteria.
[03:02] Maya: Timeline — can we have a pilot start in early Jan? Our field team is out next two weeks so Jan 4 or Jan 8 would be ideal.
[03:10] Alex: That works. We'll aim to have all materials to you before the holidays. Priya, target pilot-ready plan by Jan 7.
[03:18] Priya: Noted.
[03:20] [03:20] Ethan: On security — buyers always ask about SOC 2, encryption, KMS and SSO. Do you have a security brief we can hand to procurement?
[03:29] Alex: Yes, we have a security package. We'll share SOC2 report, KMS integration notes (K-M-S), support for SAML/SSO, and audit logs. Note — sometimes the transcription on our docs shows K-V cash instead of KV cache, sorry, internal note.
[03:43] Maya: Ha, yes we've seen the K-V cash typo before. Procurement will want to see data residency options and the retention policy too.
[03:50] Priya: We can include default retention and optional TTLs, plus private deployment options for data residency.
[03:56] Liam: There was a question from field: what's the usual lead time to spin up a dedicated GPU pool? Customers ask about 6–8 week window.
[04:03] Priya: Typical provisioning is 4–6 weeks for standard configs, 6–10 if custom hardware or on-prem. We'll put ranges in the doc.
[04:11] Maya: Great. Regarding commissions — Ethan, do you have a target % range?
[04:16] Ethan: We're thinking 8–12% for standard co-sell, higher for joint pipeline sourced by SummitBridge. We want transparency.
[04:24] Alex: We'll propose a tiered comp model — deals we source vs deals we joint-source vs deals Redwood sources. We'll include sample math in the sheet.
[04:31] Liam: Also want clarity on deal registration and crediting rules. Field needs that so reps know to coordinate.
[04:38] Alex: We'll include a short playbook: registration, handoff, pilot -> PO -> contract stages, and who owns which step.
[04:45] [04:45] Maya: One specific account — Meridian Logistics — is looking for a real-time inferencing capability for routing optimization. They asked about latency at 50 token generations and 1k token batches.
[04:57] Priya: For real-time, we'd recommend a dedicated pool with optimized kernels and KV cache. We can simulate their pattern in the benchmark. We'll ask for sample traces.
[05:07] Maya: I'll get the traces to you — could be noisy but we'll try.
[05:11] Ethan: Any red flags on compliance side if they're in EU? Data residency and GDPR considerations?
[05:16] Alex: We support regionally-deployed private control planes and can do EU-hosting for data locality. We'll document options.
[05:24] Liam: Competitor check — OpenAI sometimes wins on brand / dev ecosystem. How do we position against that?
[05:30] Priya: Emphasize predictable costs, model/version pinning, and rollout playbook — plus our optimize tooling for batching & quantization which lowers unit costs for high-volume customers.
[05:41] Maya: We also need a marketing co-sell plan — joint webinar or customer reference after a successful pilot. That helps field.
[05:48] Alex: Agreed. Let's plan a joint webinar as a later milestone after pilot success. We'll draft a go-to-market calendar.
[05:55] Ethan: One ask — can Redwood provide a short ROI calc template? Field reps want a quick $ savings estimate vs their current infra.
[06:03] Priya: We'll make a small ROI worksheet showing token costs, per-user cost, and projected savings with batching/caching.
[06:11] Maya: Perfect.
[06:13] [06:13] Alex: Okay let's recap next steps: 1) Redwood to send updated co-sell deck + commission matrix by 2026-12-20; 2) SummitBridge to send top 20 prioritized accounts by 2026-12-22; 3) Priya to deliver pilot benchmark plan by 2027-01-07; 4) exchange legal contacts for MSA addendum. Anything else?
[06:33] Ethan: Add scheduling exec intro week of 12/28.
[06:36] Alex: Noted. We'll set an invite.
[06:39] Liam: Also please include a short decision checklist for field reps; one pager that says 'green = ready for co-sell'.
[06:45] Alex: We'll add that.
[06:47] Maya: That's it from me, thanks everyone. Happy to close strong before the break.
[06:50] Priya: Thanks all.
[06:52] Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with the deck and sheet. Have a good holiday!
